back: A fixed-length vector produced by a model so that inputs with similar meaning get nearby vectors.

front: Can you compare vectors from two embedding models with the same dimension?
back: No. Each model defines its own space; cross-model distances are noise. Changing models means re-embedding everything.

front: Where is pure vector search weakest?
back: Exact tokens: part numbers, error codes, names, and negation. Pair it with keyword search.
Dot product divided by the product of lengths: the angle between vectors, from −1 to 1, ignoring magnitude.

front: Why normalise vectors to unit length?
back: Then dot product equals cosine and squared L2 = 2 − 2·cos, so all three metrics rank identically and you can use the cheapest.
<-> L2 distance, <#> negative inner product, <=> cosine distance (1 − cosine similarity).
Of the true top k (from brute force), the fraction the ANN index returned. 0.95 at k=10 means 9.5 of 10 on average.
A stack of proximity graphs: sparse upper layers for long greedy hops, a dense bottom layer searched with a beam of efSearch candidates.
M: links per node. efConstruction: candidate list size while building. efSearch: candidate list size while querying (must be ≥ k).

front: Why does HNSW want everything in RAM?
back: Search jumps to random nodes; each jump that misses memory becomes a random disk read.
k-means into nlist lists; a query compares with all centroids, then scans only the nprobe nearest lists.
96 sub-vectors of 8 dims, each stored as a 1-byte centroid id: 3,072 B → 96 B, 32× smaller, approximate distances.

front: How do you set efSearch properly?
back: Brute-force ground truth for a few hundred real queries, sweep efSearch, pick the lowest value meeting the recall target at your p99 budget.
Vectors beside their rows: transactions, joins, SQL filters, one system to back up and monitor. Good up to a well-sized single server.
ANN returns ef candidates, then the filter drops most. ef_search 40 with a 2% filter yields ~0.8 matches.
Iterative index scans (pgvector 0.8.0+), partial indexes or partitions per tenant, filter-aware engines, or exact search over the small subset.
